letters.name: ani
letters.memoryTrick: Ani looks like a little house with an arched roof and a pillar on the right. Think of saying 'Ah!' when you see your dream home — that's the open /ɑ/ sound.

letters.name: bani
letters.memoryTrick: Bani looks like a backwards number 6 with a little foot. Think of a bouncing ball going 'b-b-b' — bani starts with the same b sound as English 'ball'.

letters.name: gani
letters.memoryTrick: Gani looks like a curly spiral curling inward. Think of a galaxy swirling around — 'g' as in 'go' and 'galaxy'.

letters.name: doni
letters.memoryTrick: Doni looks like a little staircase with a door underneath. Think of a 'door' opening — the d sound is just like English 'd' in 'door'.

letters.name: eni
letters.memoryTrick: Eni looks like a sideways number 3, or a cursive lowercase 'e' turned on its side. Sounds like the 'e' in 'elephant' or 'egg' — a crisp /ɛ/ sound.

letters.name: vini
letters.memoryTrick: Vini looks like an uppercase 'R' but rounded. Think of a violin playing its first note — 'v' just like the 'v' in 'violin' and 'vine'.

letters.name: zeni
letters.memoryTrick: Zeni looks like a zigzag flash. Think of a buzzing bee making a 'zzzz' sound — same voiced z as in 'zebra' and 'buzz'.

letters.name: tani
letters.memoryTrick: Tani looks like a lowercase 'm' with a roof. It's an aspirated t — say 'top' and feel the puff of air. That puff of breath is what makes this different from the ejective ტ.

letters.name: ini
letters.memoryTrick: Ini looks like a tiny vertical snake or a candle with a flame. It makes the same 'ee' sound as 'i' in 'ski' or 'machine' — a pure /i/ vowel.

letters.name: k'ani
letters.memoryTrick: K'ani looks a bit like a ladle with a handle on the left. This is an ejective — push air out from your throat, not your lungs. Say 'k' as if you're holding your breath and popping it out sharply.

letters.name: lasi
letters.memoryTrick: Lasi looks a bit like a hook or an upside-down question mark. Think of a lion's tail curling — 'l' as in 'lion' and 'lazy'.

letters.name: mani
letters.memoryTrick: Mani looks like a mountain with a valley in the middle — two peaks joined at the base. 'M' as in 'mountain' and 'mother', same bilabial nasal sound.

letters.name: nari
letters.memoryTrick: Nari looks like a little bridge or a nose. Think of saying 'no' while pinching your nose — the same /n/ sound as English 'nose' and 'no'.

letters.name: oni
letters.memoryTrick: Oni looks like a perfect circle or ring. Think of saying 'Oh!' in surprise — it's the round /ɔ/ sound, like the 'o' in 'or' or 'organ'.

letters.name: p'ari
letters.memoryTrick: P'ari looks like an open gate with a crossbar. It's an ejective p — close your throat and pop the 'p' out sharply, with no puff of air. Almost like the p in 'spin' but even tighter.

letters.name: zhani
letters.memoryTrick: Zhani looks like a little teapot with a lid. It makes the 'zh' sound — like the 's' in 'measure' or 'pleasure', or the French 'j' in 'je'. Think of the buzzing pleasure of a warm cup of tea.

letters.name: raei
letters.memoryTrick: Raei looks like a lowercase 'h' with a little curl at the bottom. It's a rolled or tapped r — like the 'r' in Spanish 'pero' or the quick tap in 'butter' said quickly in American English.

letters.name: sani
letters.memoryTrick: Sani looks like a smooth, wavy ribbon with three curves. Think of a snake slithering with a hissing 'ssss' — same voiceless s as in 'snake' and 'sun'.

letters.name: t'ari
letters.memoryTrick: T'ari looks like a little curved hook or a shepherd's crook. This is an ejective t — close your throat, trap the air, and release the 't' sharply without a puff. Like the t in 'stop' but much tighter.

letters.name: uni
letters.memoryTrick: Uni looks like an upside-down 'U' with a little tail, or a horseshoe. Think of an owl going 'oooh' — it's the same /u/ sound as in 'boot' and 'moon'.

letters.name: pari
letters.memoryTrick: Pari looks like an open book or a tent with flaps. It's an aspirated p — say 'pill' and feel the puff of air on your palm. That puff is what separates this from the ejective პ.

letters.name: kani
letters.memoryTrick: Kani looks like a little boat with a sail. It's an aspirated k — say 'kite' and feel the puff of air. That breathy puff distinguishes this from the ejective კ.

letters.name: ghani
letters.memoryTrick: Ghani looks like a wide-open mouth. The sound is a voiced rasp deep in the throat, like the French 'r' in 'Paris' or a gentle gargle — vibrate your vocal cords while making a friction sound at the back of your mouth.

letters.name: q'ari
letters.memoryTrick: Q'ari looks like a hook reaching down into the throat. This is an ejective uvular stop — make a k sound way back where your uvula is, then eject it sharply without breath. Like a deep popping sound.

letters.name: shini
letters.memoryTrick: Shini looks like a little staircase going up. Think of someone putting a finger to their lips and saying 'shhh' — it's the same /ʃ/ sound as English 'shoe' and 'ship'.

letters.name: chini
letters.memoryTrick: Chini looks like a little chair with a curved back. It's an aspirated 'ch' — say 'chair' with the puff of air. That breathiness is what makes it different from the ejective ჭ.

letters.name: tsani
letters.memoryTrick: Tsani looks like a little curled ribbon hanging down. It's an aspirated 'ts' — like the 'ts' in 'cats' followed by a puff of air. Your tongue taps behind your teeth with extra breath.

letters.name: dzili
letters.memoryTrick: Dzili looks like a coiled spring or a zigzag. It's the voiced 'dz' — like the 'ds' in 'kids' but said as one sound. Vibrate your vocal cords as you make the ts sound.

letters.name: ts'ili
letters.memoryTrick: Ts'ili looks like a little fountain or a hand reaching up. This is an ejective 'ts' — close your throat, trap the air, and release the ts sound sharply with no breath. It pops.

letters.name: ch'ari
letters.memoryTrick: Ch'ari looks like a little hook or a whisk. This is an ejective 'ch' — trap air in your throat and pop out the ch sound sharply. Like the 'ch' in 'church' but with no breathy puff.

letters.name: khani
letters.memoryTrick: Khani looks like a little slide or a waterfall cascading down. Make the 'ch' sound in German 'Bach' or Scottish 'loch' — a rough, throaty rasp like clearing your throat softly.

letters.name: jani
letters.memoryTrick: Jani looks like a little jug or a hook with a loop. It's the voiced 'j' — just like the 'j' in English 'jump' or 'judge'. Say 'juice' and you've got it.

letters.name: haei
letters.memoryTrick: Haei looks like a simple arch or a little breath rising up. It's a gentle 'h' — just like the 'h' in English 'hello' or 'happy', a soft puff of air through an open throat.
